terms.gloss: be equal to, be a match for; cope with
terms.grammar: phrase: pār, paris, adjective, with esse and the dative
evidence: Plin. Ep. 3.17.2: cui pār esse nōn possum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 12.15: sed adhūc parēs nōn sumus (Lewis & Short: “not equal to the task”)
terms.comment: Latin says that one is, or is not, a match for the thing: a task, a worry, a grief, an enemy. Pār is first of all “equal” and, as a noun, “a pair”; pār est means “it is right, fitting” (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: be unequal to, be unable to cope with
terms.grammar: phrase: impār, imparis, adjective, with esse and the dative
evidence: Hor. C. 4.6.5: tibi mīles impār (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: in this sense perhaps not before the Augustan age; Cicero and Pliny say pār nōn esse. Its first sense is “unequal, uneven” (an odd number).

phrases.latin: exime hunc mihi scrūpulum, cui pār esse nōn possum
phrases.english: take this worry off me: I can’t cope with it

phrases.latin: cui repugnō, quoad possum, sed adhūc parēs nōn sumus
phrases.english: I fight it (my grief) as far as I can, but so far I am not equal to it

phrases.latin: Sōlus huic negōtiō pār nōn sum; adjuvā mē.
phrases.english: I can’t cope with this on my own; help me.
to be up to a task
